content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List the available project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any relevant ageing/transparency or simulation guidance documents to extract the three allowed radiator candidates, their humidity-ageing transparency losses, and any material-specific constraints or recommended scan ranges."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard ageing requirement: exclude any radiator candidate whose 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing transparency loss exceeds 10%. Record the eligible candidates and their transparency-loss values numerically where possible."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each eligible radiator, run simulate_separation at representative thicknesses across the allowed 1–6 cm range, including at least 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm if feasible. Record all resulting pion/kaon separation values."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best-performing radiator/thickness region from the coarse scan. If the maximum is not clearly at a boundary or if neighboring points are close, run additional simulations at intermediate thicknesses around the best coarse point, staying within 1–6 cm, and record the results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated eligible configurations and select the single radiator and thickness with the highest pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c while satisfying the ageing and thickness constraints. Record the winning separation value and the chosen thickness for use by the reporting module."}]}
